proposed_urls.rationale: Act 472 § 4.411 - meanings of words and phrases (definitions).
Act 472 § 4.412 - definitions generally.
Act 472 § 4.413 - additional definitions.
Act 472 § 4.414 - additional definitions.
Act 472 § 4.415 - additional definitions.
Act 472 § 4.416 - additional definitions.
Act 472 § 4.416a - resignation from office and post-office lobbying restriction; penalty.
Act 472 § 4.417 - registration forms, filing, contents, late fees, termination notice.
Act 472 § 4.418 - signed expenditure reports, amendments, food/beverage reporting, employee-lobbyist activity, preservation of statements.
Act 472 § 4.419 - preservation of accounts, bills, receipts, books, papers, documents; inspection; penalty.
Act 472 § 4.420 - accounting of lobbying and expenditures; waiver; penalty.
Act 472 § 4.421 - contingent-fee lobbying prohibition; gifts/loans; sale of information; public-official lobbying compensation; penalties.
Act 472 § 4.422 - summaries of statements and reports.
Act 472 § 4.423 - filing-determination, notice-of-error procedures, investigations and hearings.
Act 472 § 4.424 - enforcement of penalties, sworn complaints, probable-cause findings, investigation cooperation.
Act 472 § 4.425 - ordinance or resolution provision.
Act 472 § 4.426 - rulemaking authority.
Act 472 § 4.427 - civil action and criminal prosecution.
Act 472 § 4.428 - severability.
Act 472 § 4.429 - declaratory ruling or interpretive statement.
Act 472 § 4.429a - inflation adjustment of registration thresholds and penalty amounts.
Act 472 § 4.430 - effective dates of specified Act 472 sections.
Act 472 § 4.431 - repeal of MCL 4.401 to 4.410 (predecessor legislative-agents act).

notes: MI 2015 follows the same 4-level structure as MI 2010 (chapter > act > section). 23 sections in Act 472 of 1978 (Lobby Registration Act, MCL 4.411-4.431), matching MI 2010's count exactly. Single-act regime: definitions and penalties live within Act 472, so no support_chapter picks. Only repealed predecessor Act 214 of 1947 (Legislative Agents) appears in chapter 4 alongside it; no parallel executive-branch lobbying regime exists in Michigan.
